design.intro.title: Design
design.intro.lead: One accent per project, two typefaces, a hairline between everything and a line that wipes across on hover. Every sample below is the component the site itself renders.
design.colour.title: Colour
design.colour.note: Paper and ink, plus one fixed signal colour — acid lime, the same flat value across every project rather than a palette or a ramp. Switch the theme in the header to see the rest of the palette shift under it.
design.colour.projectAccents: Accent · frame, mockup, counter and triangle
design.colour.accentRationale: Six unrelated hues, then a six-step ramp of one hue — both still asked the viewer to read intensity or rotation as meaning. This is simpler: one fixed value, acid lime, used everywhere a project needs marking. It is the colour of a phosphor terminal and a highlighter pen — alert, legible, unmistakably not a corporate blue — and it never changes between projects, because the signal isn't which hue you're looking at, it's that something is live. The triangle is impossible from every angle but one; lime is the colour you would use to mark that one angle on a page. A second signature colour may join it later — the six accent slots already exist independently for exactly that — but for now there is just the one.
design.colour.mockupRoles: Mockup roles · the tones a drawn page is made of
design.type.title: Type
design.type.note: Space Grotesk for everything you read, JetBrains Mono for counters, languages and links. Sizes are fluid: every step is a clamp of the viewport, so a short screen gets smaller headings, not a scrollbar.
design.line.title: The line
design.line.note: Nothing changes colour on hover. A 2px line wipes in from the start of the word and leaves through its end; where a project owns the element, the line takes its accent.
design.line.archiveRowNote: An archive row is the same gesture at the width of the page, with the arrow coming out of the name.
design.line.archiveRowTagline: The tagline, up to the first full stop
design.mockups.title: Mockups
design.mockups.note: Each project is drawn, not screenshotted: an SVG page built at the exact pixel size of its box. Change the shape of the box and the columns, rows and lines are counted again to fill it. Point at one to see the loop it plays.
design.case.title: One project, one screen
design.case.note: A case is a counter, the name, the frame and the text, and it is at least as tall as the viewport: the frame takes whatever the words leave. This is the real component, boxed so you can see where it ends.
design.triangle.title: The impossible triangle
design.triangle.note: The mark is a Penrose triangle drawn in WebGL. On the home page it flies from the hero to the counter, through every project and into the footer, taking the accent of the one it is passing. Here it docks in the slot below: the same renderer, the same model.
design.triangle.noteContinuedPrefix: Three beams fly in and lock on load and the pointer tilts them. At
design.triangle.noteContinuedSuffix: the model is still the model: built, still, and never swapped for a flat drawing.
